title: Meet your team
why: You're on Claude iOS. Marcus leads it from SF. Lena is your teammate in London. Kai on Claude Web is your buddy, and Jun designs the screens you'll build. Say hi today so tomorrow's questions are easy to ask.

checklist.label: Read who's who above
checklist.help: The full list of teams and channels is on the 'Teams and who owns what' wiki page. Read the full page link below.

checklist.label: Post a hello in #claude-ios
checklist.help: Can't find the channel? Search Slack for claude-ios, or ask Kai, your buddy. A one line hello is plenty.

checklist.label: Reply to Kai's welcome DM
checklist.help: Kai is 16 hours ahead in Tokyo. If there is no DM yet, send one first. They are expecting it.

title: Get your gear
why: You cannot build the app until Xcode can sign it. That needs two things from two different people. This checklist is the whole morning, in order.

checklist.label: Find your laptop asset tag (sticker under the laptop, starts with ANT-)
checklist.help: Flip the laptop over. The sticker is on the bottom, near the hinge. You will need it for any IT message.

checklist.label: Connect to the VPN
checklist.help: Post in #help-it with three things: your asset tag (ANT-...), what you tried, and the exact error text. Start with BLOCKED if you cannot work. IT opens the ticket for you.

checklist.label: Install Xcode from the internal installer
checklist.help: The installer is pinned in #claude-ios. Do not use the App Store version, it lags a release behind what the project needs.

checklist.label: Accept the Apple Developer team invite
checklist.help: This does not come from IT. Marcus sends it from App Store Connect. No invite in your inbox? DM Marcus, not #help-it.

checklist.label: Install TestFlight and open the internal build
checklist.help: TestFlight access follows the Apple invite within the hour. If the build is not there after an hour, ask in #claude-ios.

title: Build the app
why: Nothing feels real until the app runs on your machine. This is the moment most new hires get stuck, and it is never their fault. The help on each step is where to look.

checklist.label: Clone the claude-ios repo
checklist.help: The repo link is pinned in #claude-ios. If you get a permission error, your GitHub org invite is still pending. Ask in #help-it.

checklist.label: Run the bootstrap script (./scripts/bootstrap)
checklist.help: It installs tools and fetches packages. If it fails on a package, run it once more before asking. If it fails twice, paste the last 20 lines in #claude-ios.

checklist.label: Open Claude.xcworkspace (not the .xcodeproj)
checklist.help: Opening the project file instead of the workspace is the number one cause of 'missing module' errors. Close it and open the workspace.

checklist.label: Build and run on an iPhone simulator
checklist.help: Signing errors here mean the Apple invite has not landed yet. Everything else, ask Lena. She has seen every build error this project can make.

checklist.label: Run the unit tests once (Cmd+U)
checklist.help: A few tests are known to be flaky on first run. Run them again. Still red? Post the test name in #claude-ios.

title: Learn the lingo
why: The iOS team has its own words. You will hear them in your first standup. Nodding along is easy. Asking is better. Knowing them is best.
facts: TF build is the nightly TestFlight build of the Claude iOS app. It goes out at 6am Pacific to the internal group.
Release train is the weekly App Store submission. It leaves every Tuesday at noon Pacific. Miss it and the change waits a week.
Crash-free rate is the share of sessions with no crash. Below 99.5% is a conversation.
scenario: Monday standup. Lena says: "Crash-free dipped to 99.2 after last night's TF build. If we can't find it today we miss the train."
task: Explain in plain words what Lena means, as if to a friend who does not work here.
rubric: A passing answer explains that last night's TestFlight build introduced crashes (crash-free rate fell below the 99.5% line) AND that if it is not fixed by Tuesday noon the weekly App Store release will go out without the fix, or be delayed a week.
hints: All three cards are in that one sentence. Take them one at a time.
TF build = last night's test build. Crash-free 99.2 = too many crashes. The train = Tuesday's App Store release.
reveal: Last night's test build is crashing more than we allow. If we cannot find the cause today, Tuesday's App Store release goes out without the fix, or waits a week.

title: Ship something tiny
why: Your first change should be boring on purpose. There is a typo in Settings: "Recieve notifications". Fix it, and you will have walked the whole path from branch to merge while nothing is at stake.

checklist.label: Branch from main: your-name/fix-receive-typo
checklist.help: Branch names are your-name/short-description. If main will not pull, you may not have the repo permission yet. Ask in #help-it.

checklist.label: Fix the string in Settings
checklist.help: Search the project for 'Recieve'. It lives in Localizable.strings. Change it in the English file only, translations follow later.

checklist.label: Take a before and after screenshot
checklist.help: UI changes always get a screenshot in the PR, even one word. Jun will ask for it anyway.

checklist.label: Open a small PR with a one paragraph why
checklist.help: Say why, not just what. 'Typo in Settings string, users see it every day' is enough.

checklist.label: Ask one reviewer and post the link in #claude-ios
checklist.help: One reviewer, not two. Lena is a safe first pick. Someone usually grabs it before lunch.

checklist.label: Wait for Xcode Cloud to go green
checklist.help: Red CI on a typo fix is almost always a flaky test. Re-run once. Still red? Ask in #claude-ios before touching anything.

title: Who owns what
why: App Store reviews land on you first. Not everything they mention is yours to fix. This one is about handing things to the right team fast.
facts: Claude iOS owns the Claude app for iPhone and iPad. Marcus Oyelaran leads it. Channel: #claude-ios.
Subscriptions owns Claude Pro billing, App Store receipts, and refunds. Priya Nair leads it. Channel: #subscriptions.
Not sure who owns something? Ask in #where-does-this-live. Nobody minds.
scenario: A one-star App Store review says: "Charged twice for Pro this month, still no refund." Marcus forwards it to you.
task: Write the short message you would post to get this looked at. Say which channel you post it in.
rubric: A passing answer routes the issue to the Subscriptions team (naming the team, Priya, or the #subscriptions channel) rather than trying to fix it in #claude-ios, and includes a short real message. Naming #subscriptions or Subscriptions/Priya is enough for the routing part.
hints: Look at the fact card about receipts and refunds. That is a different team from yours.
Billing belongs to Subscriptions. Post a short message in #subscriptions.
reveal: Post in #subscriptions: "Hi Subscriptions folks, an App Store review reports a double charge for Pro with no refund. Can someone check the receipt? I can share the review link."

title: Get heard on a call
why: Tuesday iOS planning is Marcus in SF, Jun in the office, you and Lena remote. Lag and loud rooms are real. There is a rule so quiet voices get in.
facts: Want to speak and cannot find a gap? Type "hand" in the meeting's Slack thread.
The host reads the thread queue in order before taking new speakers. First hand goes first.
Cameras are optional. Decisions get written in the thread within the hour. If it is not written, it did not happen.
scenario: Tuesday planning. Marcus and Jun are talking over each other about the new sign-in screen. You just found a bug in it that changes the plan.
task: Say what you would do to get your point in, and why the team does it that way.
rubric: A passing answer says to type 'hand' (or raise a hand) in the meeting's Slack thread and that the host reads the queue in order. It should mention the why: so remote people with lag or noise get equal air time.
hints: Card 1 is one word. Card 2 says what the host does with it.
Type 'hand' in the Slack thread. The host reads the queue in order so remote folks get equal air time.
reveal: Type 'hand' in the meeting's Slack thread. Marcus reads the queue in order. This exists so remote people get the same air time as the room.

title: Book a coffee chat
why: You will ship UI, so you will work with Design. You will touch receipts, so you will work with Subscriptions. The people you meet this week are the ones you will ask for help in week ten.

checklist.label: Pick someone outside Claude iOS above
checklist.help: Anyone not on Claude iOS counts. Jun is a great first pick, you will ship their designs.

checklist.label: Send them a DM asking for 20 minutes
checklist.help: People say yes. Something like: 'Hi, I'm new on Claude iOS. Could we do a 20 minute coffee chat this week?' Or use #coffee-roulette.

checklist.label: Put it on both calendars
checklist.help: Wednesdays are meeting free, so calendars are empty. Remember Lena and Priya are in Europe: mornings Pacific work best.

title: Beacon goes off
why: Being paged is scary the first time. The rules exist so you never have to figure it out alone at 2am. This week you are shadowing Lena's on call.
facts: When Beacon pages you: acknowledge within 10 minutes, or it escalates on its own.
Open the runbook linked in the page. If it is not fixed or understood in 30 minutes, escalate to the on call lead.
Never sit alone with a SEV1 or SEV2. Asking for help is the rule. New hires shadow for a month and are never paged alone.
scenario: It is 2:07am. Your phone buzzes: SEV2, iOS sign-in failing for 8% of users. You are shadowing Lena this week.
task: Write what you do in the first minute, what you do next, and what you do at minute 30 if it is still broken.
rubric: A passing answer covers: acknowledge the page within 10 minutes, open the runbook, and escalate to the on call lead (or loop in Lena, who they are shadowing) if not fixed or understood at 30 minutes. Mentioning they are shadowing and not alone is a bonus.
hints: Card 1 is the first minute. Card 2 is the next step and the 30 minute rule. Card 3 says who is with you.
Ack within 10 minutes. Open the runbook and loop in Lena. At 30 minutes, escalate to the on call lead.
reveal: First minute: acknowledge the page. Next: open the runbook and ping Lena, you are shadowing her. Minute 30 if still broken: escalate to the on call lead. You are never alone with a SEV2.

title: Pay it forward
why: Every note on this map was left by someone who was new once. The next iOS hire opens this same quest. Now it is your turn.
prompt: Write them a one or two sentence note. Name the stop that was hardest for you and what you would tell them.
